To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

satisfaction of the needs of autonomy, competition, relatedness, self-determined motivation (intrinsic motivation, identified regulation, and integrated regulation) and non-self-determined motivation (introjected regulation) positively predict students’ satisfaction in physical education class, whereas non-self-determined (external regulation) and non-motivation (amotivation) predict negatively satisfaction in physical education.

Satisfaction in physical education classes was predicted by satisfaction of the needs of autonomy, competition, and relatedness; self-determined forms (i.e., Intrinsic motivation, identified regulation, and integrated regulation); and one of the self-determined forms, introjected regulation.

satisfaction of the needs for relatedness and autonomy and self-determined forms (intrinsic, integrated and identified) of motivation are the best predictors of students' satisfaction within physical education classes, and the satisfaction of the need of competition only predicts satisfaction in physical education for the boys.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the satisfaction of basic needs in physical education, which is an issue that has not been studied in previous research.
the importance of the satisfaction of the basic psychological needs and self-determined motivation as a way to improve students' satisfaction in their physical education classes.
the motivational process that predicts the satisfaction of students within their physical education class.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
students' satisfaction in their physical education classes is determined by a complex set of factors, and the motivational variables are the ones which play a key role in this process.
satisfaction in physical education depends on the satisfaction of the basic psychological needs, the type of motivation and the gender of the student.

students' satisfaction in their physical education classes is predicted by their basic psychological needs, self-determination and motivational regulation, with these variables having differential weights depending on the gender of the students.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

satisfaction in physical education depends on the degree to which basic psychological needs are satisfied, the degree to which students are motivated by self-determined forms and the degree to which they are motivated by non-self-determined forms.

the satisfaction of the basic psychological needs of autonomy, competition, and relatedness, as well as the self-determined forms (intrinsic motivation, integrated regulation, and identified regulation) of motivation are positively related to the satisfaction of students in physical education.
satisfaction of basic psychological need, self-determination theory and motivation are important factors to be taken into consideration in the design of physical education programmes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

physical education teachers should promote a positive climate in their classes that encourages the satisfaction of basic needs, especially the need for relatednes, and should also foster intrinsic motivation in students, as these are two of the main factors that increase students' satisfaction in this type of classes.
the satisfaction of basic needs, self-determination and motivation are important variables to consider when trying to increase students' satisfaction in the physical education classes.

the satisfaction of the need of autonomy, intrinsic and self-determined motivation, as well as the satisfaction of the needs of competition and relatedness, are important variables to consider when trying to increase satisfaction in physical education.
